name: The Ritz Carlton Tokyo
insider_take: Perched on floors 45-53 of Tokyo Midtown Tower, this sky-high sanctuary offers unparalleled views of Mount Fuji, Imperial Palace, and the sprawling metropolis below.
whats_special: The Ritz-Carlton Tokyo holds the distinction of being one of the highest hotels in Japan, featuring the country's largest guest rooms averaging 52 square meters. The hotel's Club Level occupies the top three floors, making it literally the pinnacle of luxury hospitality in Tokyo. Art enthusiasts will appreciate the impressive collection of contemporary Japanese artwork displayed throughout the property.
pro_tip: Book a room on floors 50+ facing west for breathtaking Mount Fuji views, especially stunning at sunset. The mountain is most visible during winter months when skies are clearer.
dont_miss: The hotel's Hinoki Bar on the 45th floor, named after the Japanese cypress wood used in its construction, offers rare Japanese whiskies with panoramic city views. Just steps away, explore the Suntory Museum of Art and 21_21 Design Sight in Tokyo Midtown, plus the traditional Mohri Garden at the tower's base provides a serene contrast to the urban energy above.
pros: Spectacular panoramic views of Tokyo skyline and Mount Fuji from upper floors
World-class spa and wellness facilities with traditional Japanese treatments
Exceptional fine dining restaurants including Michelin-starred options
Premium location in Midtown Tokyo with easy access to shopping and business districts
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive positioning
Formal atmosphere may not suit all travelers seeking casual experiences
